summary: Baileys fork aliases libsignal to unofficial scope at @latest
details: package.json for @kxa/xbails@0.0.5 declares its libsignal dependency via an npm alias to an unofficial scope pinned to a mutable tag: "libsignal": "npm:@bellaxchuu/libsignal-node@latest". The official libsignal-node used by Baileys is published under WhiskeySockets; @bellaxchuu is an unrelated third-party scope. Because the alias uses the @latest tag with no version pin and no integrity constraint, every `npm install` of @kxa/xbails resolves whatever bytes that scope currently publishes and executes any lifecycle scripts (preinstall/install/postinstall) contained in them on the installer's host. The manifest itself is the install-time execution vector: the shipped code does not need to be malicious for arbitrary third-party code to run during install, and the resolved payload can change at any time without a new release of this package.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
